text: A quote is a promise about cost, made before the job exists.
Every quote has four parts: material, labour, setup and margin.
Material comes from the bill of materials, scrap included, at today's cost.
Labour is hours times a shop rate, not the wage. The rate must recover overheads.
Now the trap. Margin and markup are different numbers.
Example: on a $141.99 cost, a 35% markup gives $191.69. A 35% margin gives $218.45.
Spread setup over the real batch, or small batches lose money.
For most small job shops, quote where jobs and stock live, so each quote meets its real cost.
